title: Platform systems & services — how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, and roadmap
author: Maya Patel
summary: Consolidated platform engineering reference: system inventory, common how-tos, canonical dashboards & alerts, operational runbooks, retrospectives template, and near-term roadmap for platform systems and services.
content:
Introduction:
This page is the canonical eng-platform reference for systems and services: how-to procedures, dashboard and alert definitions, runbooks for common incidents, retrospective guidance, and the roadmap for platform improvements. Use this page for operational onboarding, incident response, and planning.

Scope:
- Applies to all production and staging services owned by Platform Systems & Services (k8s-cluster-manager, routing-proxy, telemetry-ingest, batch-scheduler, secrets-operator, infra-api).
- Includes hosted/shared infrastructure used by Redwood product teams (shared VPCs, observability pipelines, and deployment tooling).

1) System inventory (overview)
- k8s-cluster-manager — self-service cluster provisioning and policy controller. Owner: platform-cluster-team. SLA: 99.9% control-plane API availability for managed clusters.
- routing-proxy — edge routing + rate limiting for hosted API. Owner: platform-networking. Target P50 latency < 30ms for 1-token RPC.
- telemetry-ingest — metric & trace collection pipeline (Prometheus -> Thanos; Jaeger -> Tempo). Owner: observability-team. Retention: 90 days metrics, 365 days traces (cold storage).
- batch-scheduler — scheduled inference jobs and offline evaluation workers. Owner: batch-team. Autoscale policy: min 2, max 200 workers per region.
- secrets-operator — centralized KMS/HSM integration and sync to clusters. Owner: security-infra. Compliance: FIPS-validated KMS for restricted customers.

2) How-tos (common procedures)
A. Deploy a service to staging (standard path)
1. Create PR against infra/overlays/<service>/staging with image tag and config changes.
2. Run local lint: ./scripts/ci-lint.sh && ./scripts/k8s-validate.sh staging.
3. Create ephemeral canary via: ./tools/deploy_canary.sh --service <service> --image <tag> --namespace staging-canary.
4. Validate health: curl -sS https://staging-canary.<domain>/healthz -> status: 200 and /metrics shows 1/1 up.
5. Promote using rolling deploy pipeline (CI job: promote-staging-to-prod).

B. Canary rollout checklist
- Traffic target: 5% first 10m, 25% next 20m, 100% if no errors after 30m.
- Validate: error rate < 0.5% and 95th latency within 10% of baseline.
- If errors spike: rollback immediately (see runbook).

C. Add a dashboard (minimal required widgets)
- Create Grafana dashboard under folder /Platform/System/<service>. Required panels:
  - Overview: success-rate, request-rate (RPS), p50/p90/p99 latency, error-budget burn chart.
  - Resource: CPU/GPU utilization, memory, pod counts.
  - Infra: node failures, pod restarts, OOMs.
- Dashboard metadata: description, owner, and alert links. Set dashboard ownership to service owner alias.

3) Dashboards & Alerts (canonical definitions)
SLO & alerting principles:
- SLOs should measure user-visible behavior (e.g., request success and latency) and align with product-level commitments.
- Prefer composite alerts (errors + latency + saturation) to reduce noise.
- Every alert must include: severity, pager escalation, runbook link, and remediation steps.

Example alert table:
| Alert name | Condition | Severity | Pager | Runbook |
| routing-proxy-5xx-spike | > 1% 5xx for 5m and RPS > 10 | sev2 | oncall-routing | /runbooks/routing-proxy-5xx.json |
| telemetry-ingest-backlog | ingestion lag > 30m for 10m | sev2 | oncall-observability | /runbooks/telemetry-backlog.json |
| k8s-controlplane-unavailable | kube-apiserver 5m unreachable | sev1 | platform-oncall | /runbooks/k8s-controlplane.json |
| secrets-sync-failure | sync failures > 3 in 10m | sev3 | security-infra | /runbooks/secrets-operator.json |

Alert thresholds (summary):
- Sev1: immediate pager, critical customer impact, aim for TTR < 30m.
- Sev2: pager during business hours, notify via Slack and oncall rotation; aim for TTR < 2h.
- Sev3: ticket to team, revisit in next sprint.

4) Runbooks (canonical incident flow)
Every runbook must follow this structure: symptoms -> impact assessment -> mitigation steps -> verification -> post-incident tasks -> owner & comms.

Example: routing-proxy-5xx runbook (summary)
Symptoms:
- Spike in 5xxs, customers reporting failed requests, elevated error budget burn.
Impact assessment:
- Determine blast radius: which routes? which customers? escalate to CS if customer-facing token involved.
Mitigation steps (ordered):
1. Acknowledge incident in Incident Slack channel and set status page to investigating.
2. Roll traffic to fallback model variant or lower tier routing via feature-flag: ffctl set routing-proxy.fallback=true.
3. Scale up routing-proxy pods: kubectl scale deployment routing-proxy -n prod --replicas=50.
4. If 5xx cause is upstream (backend service), perform targeted failover: update route weights.
5. If memory/OOM suspected, increase pod memory and restart pods with rolling update.
Verification:
- Confirm 5xx rate < 0.5% and user-facing error reports stop.
Post-incident tasks:
- Run postmortem template, identify root cause, and schedule remediation (bugfix or capacity change).

Escalation matrix (short):
- Platform oncall -> Service owner -> Team lead -> Head of Platform -> Security/Legal (if customer data impacted).

5) Retrospectives & blameless postmortems
Template (use in-page with headings):
- Summary (1-2 sentences)
- Timeline of events (timestamps, actors)
- Root cause analysis (technical + process)
- Contributing factors (environmental, tooling, personnel)
- Remediation plan (owners, due dates)
- Follow-up verification steps
Retrospective cadence: for sev1/sev2 incidents run a 1-week follow-up to validate remediations.

6) Platform roadmap (Q2–Q4 2026 highlights)
Q2 2026:
- Migrate telemetry-ingest to Thanos v2: reduce storage costs by 18%. Owner: observability-team.
- Sidecarless secrets sync MVP for private deployments. Owner: security-infra.
Q3 2026:
- Launch autoscaling improvements for batch-scheduler (predictive scheduler using recent job traces). Owner: batch-team.
- Routing-proxy: programmable rate-limiting rules and per-tenant quotas. Owner: platform-networking.
Q4 2026:
- Unified dashboard hub: single pane for product teams with RBAC and embedded runbooks. Owner: observability-team + platform-ui.

Roadmap notes:
- Each roadmap item has a PRD and an RFC in /confluence/eng-platform/decision-records. Prioritization is driven by measured pain from incidents and usage growth.

7) Team wiki & ownership
- Onboard checklist: new engineers must complete the "Platform Onboarding" checklist (link) and shadow on-call twice within first 30 days.
- Ownership registry: update OWNERS.md in each service repo and the central oncall-roster spreadsheet (link).
- Documentation standards: all service docs must include a short summary, contact, SLOs, dashboard link, and runbook link.

8) Operational hygiene & quarterly tasks
- Quarterly capacity planning: platform-sre to publish forecast and required commits two weeks before quarter end.
- Dashboard review: owners to review alert thresholds and panels quarterly to reduce alert fatigue.
- Game days: run 1-2 game days per quarter to validate runbooks and fallbacks.

Appendix (commands and snippets)
- Promote canary: ./tools/promote.sh --service routing-proxy --from staging-canary --to prod
- Check pipeline status: ci status get --pipeline promote-staging-to-prod
- Grafana dashboard export: grafana-cli export-dashboard --uid <uid> --file routing-proxy.json
